papers.title: The development of cool and hot inhibitory control from late childhood to young adulthood: An ERP study.
papers.reason: The paper directly studies developmental changes in inhibitory control using ERP, making it highly relevant to neural and behavioural mechanisms of executive function.

papers.title: Visual-linguistic cues in manual communication: Neural and behavioral responses to Mouthings in sign-naïve perception.
papers.reason: The study uses EEG and mentions cognitive control demands, but its core contribution is about visual-linguistic processing rather than executive function modelling or assessment.

papers.title: Associations Between Individual Differences in Cognitive Control Capacity and Multitasking Performance
papers.reason: The paper links individual differences in cognitive control capacity to multitasking behaviour, fatigue, and EEG dynamics, making it strongly relevant to executive function assessment and modelling.

papers.title: A Quantitative Meta-Analysis of Neural Response to Cognitive Challenge in Children and Adults With a History of Childhood Maltreatment.
papers.reason: The meta-analysis concerns neural responses to cognitive challenge in humans, which may inform models of cognitive control, though the executive-function specificity is unclear from the available information.

papers.title: Deep TMS modulates neurovascular responses and enhances dual-task computation in healthy adults
papers.reason: The study examines prefrontal and anterior cingulate modulation of dual-task cognitive control using stimulation and fNIRS, giving it clear but intervention-focused relevance to executive function.

papers.title: Multimodal evidence associated with 20Hz rTMS in AD: neuroaxonal injury reduction, neural oscillatory rebalancing, and multilayer network integration.
papers.reason: The paper appears to involve multimodal neural evidence in Alzheimer's disease, but the title does not indicate executive-function modelling, task-based assessment, or clinical classification.

papers.title: Transfer-Related Cognitive and Learning Profiles Across Predominant MOBA Roles in Novice Esports Players
papers.reason: The paper measures EEG attention, working-memory theta, and cognitive load during a dual n-back task in humans, but its main focus is exploratory esports role differences rather than modelling or clinical assessment.

papers.title: Prefrontal cortical morphometric covariance and cognitive task performance in healthy young adults: an exploratory analysis of Human Connectome Project data
papers.reason: The paper examines associations between prefrontal cortical structure and executive-function tasks including working memory, inhibitory control, and reward-based decision-making, though findings are exploratory and mostly not robust.
